text:
maria.g: prepping to publish SDKs (py/ts) 1.4.0. changelog + deprecation note for legacy sync client added. planning to push at 15:00 PT during the weekly change window. anyone on call?
sam.k: I'm on until 16:30 PT, can monitor publishes and smoke tests.
jen.w: I'll update the docs site after publish. remind me to run the docs build.
alex.r: quick preflight: have we bumped the peer deps and updated the monorepo pin matrix? also confirm release notes include migration steps for sync->async clients.
maria.g: yes to both. pin matrix updated in infra repo under packages/pins/ (PR #482). migration snippet added: ````js
// old sync client
const c = new RedwoodSyncClient(apiKey)
// new async client
const c = await RedwoodClient.create({ apiKey })
````
jen.w: can we add a short deprecation blurb: "legacy sync clients deprecated, security fixes only after 2026-06-01" — customers get 90d notice.
sam.k: agreed. also can we publish py with a dist-tag `canary` first, then shift `latest` after 30m smoke? avoids immediate mass adoption.
maria.g: plan: 15:00 PT - publish canary -> run smoke tests (api gen, chat simple convo, embeddings), 15:30 PT - promote to latest if green. anyone object?
alex.r: no objections. note: for npm we'll set dist-tag canary then `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@1.4.0 latest` on green. for pip we'll upload wheel with `--pre` tag? pip doesn't have dist-tags; we'll use prerelease like `1.4.0rc1` for canary then final `1.4.0`.
release-bot: [release-bot] queued: create-release 1.4.0 (py/ts) — changelog link https://git.internal/redwood/releases/1.4.0
15:00 PT
pkg-bot: published: @redwood/sdk 1.4.0-canary -> npm registry (sha: b7f9c3)
pkg-bot: uploaded: redwood_sdk-1.4.0rc1-py3-none-any.whl -> PyPI test (pkg index)
jen.w: starting docs build now.
sam.k: running smoke tests against canary (ts/py).
sam.k: TS basic chat ok, embeddings ok.
sam.k: PY basic chat ok, embeddings ok. latency within range.
alex.r: running integration test suite against canary in staging (full convo scenario).
15:18 PT
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] smoke/test-run completed: 42/44 checks passed. failures: integration/test-long-stream (timeout) and ts-client-e2e (unexpected truncated streaming).
sam.k: saw that streaming truncation in one run, might be flaky. retrying full run.
15:25 PT
alex.r: re-ran integration, reproduces truncated streaming on TS client path when using SSE in edge region. suspect the new chunking logic in 1.4.0.
maria.g: OK don't promote to latest. we need a rollback for TS and continue with PyPI promotion? pros/cons.
jen.w: docs already built against canary artifacts; we should hold publishing docs until final is green.
sam.k: we can promote PyPI final if py tests are green and TS stays canary. but customers using combined bundles might get mixed versions. risk note.
alex.r: recommend rollback TS to 1.3.9 and push a hotfix branch for stream handling; keep py release as 1.4.0 (final).
maria.g: decision: promote PyPI 1.4.0 final now; rollback/unpublish npm 1.4.0-canary and publish a 1.3.9 patch for TS. notify customers and update pin guidance.
release-bot: [release-bot] promoting: redwood_sdk 1.4.0 -> PyPI latest
pkg-bot: uploaded: redwood_sdk-1.4.0-py3-none-any.whl -> PyPI (sha: a3d9f2)
pkg-bot: npm package @redwood/sdk 1.4.0-canary remains on dist-tag `canary` (not latest).
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] PyPI promotion successful.
alex.r: creating TS rollback PR to revert commit that introduced chunking change and bump to 1.3.9. PR #495.
sam.k: I'll unpublish the canary tag from npm to reduce confusion: `npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk canary` and then publish 1.3.9 with `patch` tag.
15:47 PT
pkg-bot: npm dist-tag removed: @redwood/sdk canary
pkg-bot: published: @redwood/sdk 1.3.9 -> npm (sha: c1f4e0)
alex.r: TS 1.3.9 published, requesting validation.
sam.k: running TS e2e against 1.3.9, streaming tests pass.
jen.w: docs build paused; updating changelog entry to note TS rollback and PyPI final push, adding migration guidance and incident blurb.
maria.g: will send a short customer-facing note: what changed, downgrade/pin advice: "If you saw streaming truncation, pin to @redwood/sdk@^1.3.9 until 1.4.1 ships."
alex.r: suggest adding package-lock/poetry lock guidance: set exact pin in lockfile, or for npm recommend `~1.3.9` not caret.
sam.k: I'll add an internal alert to monitoring that looks for sudden installs of 1.4.0 in the next 72h.
release-bot: [release-bot] changelog updated, release notes appended with rollback details.
maria.g: thanks all. follow-ups: 1) ship TS hotfix branch tomorrow AM, 2) run extended streaming QA, 3) schedule 1.4.1 for next change window.
jen.w: noted. I'll merge docs changes after final validation. :thumbsup:
alex.r: +1.
sam.k: closing thread once docs merged and monitoring alarms in place.
maria.g: closing — great teamwork.
